title: Inside the MOSFET: Gate, Oxide, and Body Explained

segments.text: What separates the gate from the silicon body?
The gate, made of metal or polysilicon, sits on that insulating frosting.
Together they act as a planar capacitor: one plate is the gate, the other is the semiconductor beneath the oxide.
When you apply a voltage to the gate, an electric field shoots through the oxide and reaches the silicon surface, rearranging charges there.
It pulls electrons toward the interface and pushes holes away, preparing a region ready for conduction.
This tiny stack is the heart of the MOSFET and has been refined since the late 1950s.
